concept.name: Performance anxiety
concept.definition: Anxiety triggered by the requirement to perform under evaluation or pressure, activating the sympathetic fight-or-flight response (racing heart, tremor, dry mouth) and degrading execution. In trading it appears around real-money exposure, position sizing, drawdowns, or being observed, and is related to choking under pressure in skilled performance.
concept.intuition: The setup is the same one you nailed in simulation a hundred times, but with real money and people watching, your hands shake and you cannot pull the trigger.
concept.mechanics: Anticipation of evaluation raises arousal beyond the zone of optimal performance, narrowing attention and disrupting well-learned decision routines; it affects even highly experienced performers and can begin long before the event. Standard mitigations are preparation, breathing and attentional routines, graded exposure, and self-monitoring.
concept.failure_modes: It corrupts execution precisely on high-stakes trades - hesitation on entries, premature exits, refusal to size per plan - and can generalize into chronic avoidance of valid risk. Suppressing symptoms without addressing sizing or process rarely works.
concept.misconceptions: Performance anxiety is not a sign of incompetence; elite performers across domains report it. Nor is all arousal harmful - moderate arousal can aid performance; the problem is excessive evaluative pressure.
concept.example: A trader who executes flawlessly in a demo account repeatedly exits funded positions minutes after entry, well before either stop or target, whenever the daily P&L is visible.
